draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Bhandardara! Mount Kalsubai rises above town at 1646 m, the highest peak in Maharashtra, with a temple right on top. Down below, the Wilson dam on the Pravara river has been holding back the lake since 1910.
draft.hungryLine: Try home-cooked village fare at least once, and Hotel Vaibhav near the MTDC resort is a tourist favourite for local dishes.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Start at Wilson dam and the Umbrella falls below it, then drive out to Randha falls, where the water drops 45 m.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Go boating on Bhandardara lake, or book a tent stay right by the lakeside.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Amruteshwar temple in nearby Ratanwadi is over 1200 years old, one of twelve Shiva temples built by King Jhanjha.

spots.name: Wilson dam
spots.detail: Short drive · Built in 1910, with Umbrella falls just below

spots.name: Randha falls
spots.detail: 10 km from Shendi Village · Water drops a full 45 m

spots.name: Amruteshwar temple
spots.detail: 17 km away · An intricately carved 9th-century Shiva temple in Ratanwadi

legends.title: Shivaji's favourite
legends.body: Ratangad, above the town, is said to have been Chhatrapati Shivaji's favourite fort. Today it's a trekkers' delight.

tips.title: Come in the monsoon for the falls.
tips.body: Umbrella falls only shows up in the monsoon or when the dam gates are opened.

tips.title: Order your thali ahead.
tips.body: Off-peak, Hotel Kaka wants thali orders by phone in advance, and you might wait up to an hour.

story.title: Shilahara stonework
story.body: Rulers of the Shilahara dynasty built the carved Amruteshwar temple in Ratanwadi. It's one of twelve Shiva temples built by King Jhanjha.

story.title: Forts on the hills
story.body: Ratangad and Harishchandragad forts stand above the town. Ratangad is remembered as Shivaji's favourite fort.

story.title: Wilson dam
story.body: Wilson dam went up on the Pravara river in 1910. Arthur Lake and the Umbrella falls are part of what it created.

story.title: Holiday village
story.body: Bhandardara is now a holiday resort village about 185 km from Mumbai and 73 km from Nashik. People come for boating, birdwatching, trekking and pilgrimage.

food.name: Hotel Vaibhav
food.detail: Close to the MTDC resort, popular with tourists for typical local dishes

food.name: Hotel Yashanjali
food.detail: Inside the MTDC resort, veg and non-veg food with local flavour and purified drinking water

food.name: Hotel Kaka
food.detail: In the market area, the cleanest spot in town, serving only Gujarati thali
